svg.aria-label: The layer epigenetic regulation adds to transcriptional control: DNA wound on nucleosomes so that a regulatory sequence may exist yet not be accessible, the three mechanisms of remodelling, histone modification and DNA methylation, and the criteria separating transient control, maintenance through cell division and transmission across generations.
svg.text: A Existing and being accessible are not the same
DNA wraps the histone octamer about 1.7 times
a sequence inside that turn is not exposed to a transcription factor
the same regulatory sequence is open in one cell type
and closed in another: presence does not mean availability
B Three mechanisms set the state
chromatin remodelling
ATP-driven sliding or eviction of nucleosomes
histone modification
acetyl, methyl, phosphate groups on the tails
acetylation tends to open; some methylations close
DNA methylation
methyl on the cytosine of a CpG
a methylated promoter region is usually silent
C What the word covers: two conditions
1 expression state changes with no change in DNA sequence
2 that state survives cell division
both are required, which is what the three rows below separate
D Three categories, kept distinct
transient control factors switched on and off by a signal; not inherited through division, so NOT epigenetic
maintenance through division a differentiated cell keeps its identity; the proper scope of the term
across generations shown only in limited cases such as imprinting; broader claims rest on weak evidence
